title: The integral scalar extension is well defined, a derived limit, and O_E-linear
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime and $E\subset L$ finite extensions of $\Ql$ ($L$ finite over $\Ql$, $E$ a subfield of $L$ containing $\Ql$) [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E,\mathcal O_L$, uniformizers $\varpi_E,\varpi_L$ and finite coefficient rings $A_{E,m}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m$, $A_{L,m}=\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^m$ ($m\geq1$). The restriction of $|\cdot|_L$ to $E$ is an absolute value extending $|\cdot|_\ell$, hence equals $|\cdot|_E$ [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value]; so $\mathcal O_E=\mathcal O_L\cap E\subset\mathcal O_L$ and $|\varpi_E|_L<1$, i.e. $\varpi_E\in\varpi_L\mathcal O_L$. Hence $\varpi_E^m\mathcal O_L\subset\varpi_L^m\mathcal O_L$, and the inclusion $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$ induces ring maps $\iota_m:A_{E,m}\to A_{L,m}$ commuting with the transition maps $A_{E,m+1}\to A_{E,m}$, $A_{L,m+1}\to A_{L,m}$. Let $Y$ be a scheme with small pro-etale site $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and for a ring $A$ let $A_Y$ be the constant sheaf of rings, functorial in $A$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. For $F\in\{E,L\}$ let $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,Y}=\varprojlim_m(A_{F,m})_Y$ be the completed coefficient sheaf with projections $\pi^F_m:\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,Y}\to(A_{F,m})_Y$, restriction of scalars $\operatorname{Res}^F_m$ along $\pi^F_m$ and derived category $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_F)$ of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,Y}$-modules [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Put $\rho_m=(\iota_m)_Y\circ\pi^E_m:\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}\to(A_{L,m})_Y$; then $\rho_m$ is $\rho_{m+1}$ followed by $(A_{L,m+1})_Y\to(A_{L,m})_Y$.

For a complex $P$ of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$-modules put $P_{L,m}=P\otimes_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}}(A_{L,m})_Y$, the termwise change of rings along $\rho_m$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], a complex of $(A_{L,m})_Y$-modules. The transition $(A_{L,m+1})_Y\to(A_{L,m})_Y$ induces a map of complexes $P_{L,m+1}\to P_{L,m}$; since $\pi^L_m$ is $\pi^L_{m+1}$ followed by that transition, it is a map $t_m:\operatorname{Res}^L_{m+1}P_{L,m+1}\to\operatorname{Res}^L_mP_{L,m}$ of complexes of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,Y}$-modules [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Write

$$
 \operatorname{Rlim}^{\mathrm c}_m\operatorname{Res}^L_mP_{L,m}=\operatorname{Cone}\Bigl(1-s:\prod_m\operatorname{Res}^L_mP_{L,m}\to\prod_m\operatorname{Res}^L_mP_{L,m}\Bigr)[-1],\qquad (c_m)_m\mapsto(c_m-t_m(c_{m+1}))_m,
$$

on the termwise countable products of sheaves of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,Y}$-modules [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. A K-flat complex is meant in the sense of [def-pc-kflat-complex] for the ringed site $(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y})$.

Then:
1. If $u:P\to P'$ is a quasi-isomorphism between K-flat complexes of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$-modules with flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], the induced maps $P_{L,m}\to P'_{L,m}$ are quasi-isomorphisms for every $m$, and the induced map $\operatorname{Rlim}^{\mathrm c}_m\operatorname{Res}^L_mP_{L,m}\to\operatorname{Rlim}^{\mathrm c}_m\operatorname{Res}^L_mP'_{L,m}$ is a quasi-isomorphism.
2. Consequently, choosing for every $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ a quasi-isomorphism $P_K\to K$ with $P_K$ K-flat with flat terms [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], $K\mapsto\operatorname{Rlim}^{\mathrm c}_m\operatorname{Res}^L_m(P_K)_{L,m}$ (on a morphism $K\to K'$, the map induced by the morphism $P_K\to P_{K'}$ of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ it determines) is a well-defined additive functor $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)\to D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_L)$, independent of the choice of the resolutions up to unique isomorphism of functors compatible with their natural comparison isomorphisms on K-flat representatives; it commutes with the shift; and each value is a derived limit [def-weil-derived-limit] in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_L)$ of the tower $(\operatorname{Res}^L_m(P_K)_{L,m},t_m)_m$.
3. The functor of (2) is $\mathcal O_E$-linear: for $a\in\mathcal O_E$ and a morphism $f$ of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ it sends $af$ to $a$ times the image of $f$, where $\mathcal O_E$ acts on the Hom groups of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ and, through $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$, of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_L)$ by the constant global sections [lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category].

The well-definedness argument is the one of dag node lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined, for the ring maps rho_m in place of pi_m.

proof.text: Write $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$, $S=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,Y}$ and $B_m=(A_{L,m})_Y$. The absolute-value uniqueness in [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value] identifies the restriction from $L$ with that on $E$. By the definition of uniformizer in [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], $\varpi_E\in\mathfrak m_L=\varpi_L\mathcal O_L$, so $\varpi_E^m\mathcal O_L\subseteq\varpi_L^m\mathcal O_L$. Thus the quotient map sends the class of $a$ to its class modulo $\varpi_L^m$; reducing either before or after this map gives that same class. Functorial constant sheafification and the limit projections give the asserted compatible $\rho_m$. The transition on tensor generators is $x\otimes b\mapsto x\otimes\bar b$; the equality $\rho_m=\mathrm{red}\circ\rho_{m+1}$ makes this balanced. Restricting along the projections from $S$ makes it $S$-linear. All identities descend from presheaf tensors to their sheafifications.

source.place: Termwise coefficient change preceding Tag 06YT; elementary quotient and tensor identities

proof.text: Construct the ordinary coefficient-change functor by sectionwise scalar extension followed by sheafification, so its objects and maps are the specified sheafified tensors. The public functor is uniquely fixed by equality to this constructed functor. Its proved equality and comparison isomorphism identify the tensor sections and transition maps with the explicit sheafified constructions; no arbitrary existence data is chosen. Apply [lem-pur-change-of-rings-kflat-quasi-iso] on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ to the sheaf-ring map $\rho_m:R\to B_m$. It gives that $u\otimes_R B_m$ is a quasi-isomorphism. This needs no flatness of $B_m$ over $R$. Restriction of scalars in [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] preserves the underlying abelian sheaf, kernels, images and cokernels: these acquire the restricted action, so cohomology also has the same underlying sheaf and restriction preserves this quasi-isomorphism. The resulting maps $a_m$ commute strictly with transitions, since both orders send $x\otimes b$ to $u(x)\otimes\bar b$.

For any resulting tower $C_m=\operatorname{Res}^L_m P_{L,m}$ put $A=\prod_m C_m$ and $v=1-s$. By [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact] and [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence] (2), this termwise product represents the derived-category product. The rotated cone triangle of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] for $v$ is a Roos triangle, so $T(P)=\operatorname{Cone}(v)[-1]$ is a derived limit in exactly the sense of [def-weil-derived-limit]. For the strict tower map of step 2, $g=\prod_m a_m$ satisfies $gv=v\prime g$. The diagonal map on the two cone summands gives a morphism of Roos triangles. All its level maps are isomorphisms in the derived category; the two-out-of-three isomorphism criterion for a morphism of distinguished triangles [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] says that its cone map is an isomorphism. Applying every cohomology functor proves that $T(u)$ is a quasi-isomorphism, completing (1). The Lean proof reuses the proved Roos-invariance and derived-limit lemmas of [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined] for the target completed-coefficient module category.

Coefficient extension and restriction are additive functors of module sheaves. Form their termwise countable product and the natural endomorphism one minus the transition shift. Applying this additive module functor termwise to complexes agrees naturally with the product of the individual termwise functors, by the universal property of products. This comparison intertwines the two one-minus-shift maps. The diagonal mapping-cone construction and shift by minus one are additive. The universal-property comparison identifies this cone functor with the specified Roos functor, whose map uses homotopyCofiber.mapArrowHom; the latter agrees with mappingCone.map on both summands. Hence the actual complex-level scalar extension is additive.

proof.text: Use the proved good-complex localization lemma of [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined] for the source completed-coefficient module category. Its proof uses the functorial flat resolution of [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] and the functorial-left-resolutions criterion; no intervening homotopy-subcategory presentation is needed. Step 3 shows that the specified Roos functor followed by Q inverts the induced quasi-isomorphisms. The localization universal property [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] produces F and its comparison e. Good complexes are closed under binary biproducts: tensoring preserves finite sums and flat terms are closed under finite sums. Additivity descends because the localization functor is additive and essentially surjective; preserve zero and transport the binary-biproduct product cone to prove binary-product preservation. Fully faithful precomposition gives the unique comparison isomorphism compatible with e and any e-prime.

proof.text: For any good complex P and supplied isomorphism q:QP ≅ K, the composite m=(F(q))⁻¹ followed by e at P gives F(K) ≅ QT(P). Step 3 supplies the derived-limit property for QT(P). Transport its Roos-triangle witness along m, using the proved derived-limit transport lemma of [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined]. This gives the two assertions for every supplied model, without choosing chain-map lifts for arbitrary derived morphisms.

proof.text: Shift preserves flat terms, and K-flatness follows from the natural comparison between tensor with a shifted complex and the shifted tensor. Termwise additive functors commute coherently with all integer shifts. Transfer these comparisons to the product functor by the product comparison of step 4. For a natural transformation commuting with shifts, the standard mappingCone.shiftIso and the comparisons of its source and target define a shift comparison for the cone functor. Verify naturality and the zero and addition coherence equations on the two cone summands; the only signs are the powers of minus one, whose multiplication is controlled by the addition law. Shift by minus one also commutes with all shifts, so the actual Roos functor has CommShift over the integers. Transfer this structure to the localization lift using shift stability of the induced quasi-isomorphisms and the localization universal property.

source.place: Explicit shifted-cone signs in Tag 08TC, using the cochain shift convention

proof.text: Constant sections give $\mathcal O_E$-linear structures on both module-sheaf categories, on the target through $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$: sums and composition are bilinear sectionwise. By [lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category], these induce the asserted scalar actions on the derived categories and linear localization functors. For $a\in\mathcal O_E$, tensor balancing gives $(ax)\otimes b=x\otimes\iota_m(a)b$. Thus $T(a\,\mathrm{id}_P)=a\,\mathrm{id}_{T(P)}$, on both product and cone summands, since the $S$-action projects to $a\bmod\varpi_L^m$ in every coordinate. These are equal natural endomorphisms on K-flat representatives. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] (3), their descended endomorphisms coincide on every object: $F(a\,\mathrm{id}_K)=a\,\mathrm{id}_{F(K)}$. Hence $F(af)=F((a\,\mathrm{id})f)=aF(f)$; conjugating by the $S$-linear $i_K$ preserves this equality. This proves (3) without imposing an unrelated characteristic $p$ or using the narrower constructible-linearity lemma. The Lean action definition is proved equal to this canonical fully faithful lift. Its named component formula and a parametric localization comparison establish linearity before substituting the concrete descended functor.

lean.statement: theorem integralScalarExtensionWellDefined : (∀ (P P' : (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).FullSubcategory) (f : P.obj ⟶ P'.obj), QuasiIso f → (∀ n : ℕ, QuasiIso ((integralScalarFiniteComplex l E L ι Y n).map f)) ∧ QuasiIso ((integralScalarComplexFunctor l E L ι Y).map f)) ∧ ∃ (F : DerivedCategory (integralTowerModules l E Y) ⥤ DerivedCategory (integralTowerModules l L Y)) (e : integralOperationsGoodLocalization l E Y ⋙ F ≅ integralScalarOnGood l E L ι Y), F.Additive ∧ Nonempty (F.CommShift ℤ) ∧ (∀ (F' : DerivedCategory (integralTowerModules l E Y) ⥤ DerivedCategory (integralTowerModules l L Y)) (e' : integralOperationsGoodLocalization l E Y ⋙ F' ≅ integralScalarOnGood l E L ι Y), ∃! α : F ≅ F', isoWhiskerLeft (integralOperationsGoodLocalization l E Y) α ≪≫ e' = e) ∧ (∀ (K : DerivedCategory (integralTowerModules l E Y)) (P : (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).FullSubcategory) (_q : DerivedCategory.Q.obj P.obj ≅ K), Nonempty (F.obj K ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((integralScalarComplexFunctor l E L ι Y).obj P.obj)) ∧ integralOperationsDerivedLimitProperty l L Y ((integralScalarTowerFunctor l E L ι Y).obj P.obj) (F.obj K)) ∧ (∀ (a : Padic.coefficientExtensionIntegers l E) (K K' : DerivedCategory (integralTowerModules l E Y)) (f : K ⟶ K'), F.map ((integralScalarDerivedAction l E Y a).app K ≫ f) = (integralScalarDerivedAction l L Y (integralScalarIntegerInclusion l E L ι a)).app (F.obj K) ≫ F.map f)
